design:
Decisions with the operator, 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13:
- Current project only. A query never returns another project's rows, and the Hub enforces this rather than trusting each query to filter.
- Queries only: no stored tables or materialised datasets in this slice.
- Free text is queryable (agent output, trace tool arguments and results, model messages, command lines, message, queue and checkpoint text), and queries can match regular expressions, so a dashboard can count leaks or occurrences in conversations.
- Table panels show what the query returns in full, free text included; nothing is masked (2026-11-13: the screen is local, and masking would defeat finding a leak).
- Never queryable: credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers), this machine's paths (project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints), and other projects' rows.
- The reference of what can be queried is generated by the Hub from the version that is running. What the data means and its traps go in a vault note that agents read and add to.
- The note is seeded in every project, idempotently, at Hub startup and at project creation, and never overwrites what agents added (2026-11-13).
- Charts are a fixed set of kinds the app draws in its own colours, type and light and dark themes. Rejected: agent-written visual code.
- Saving a dashboard checks the chart kind and the never-queryable boundary but does not run its queries; the tool guidance tells agents to check each query with run_dashboard_query first, and a failing panel shows its error when opened (2026-11-13).
- A dashboard runs its queries when opened and when Refresh is pressed; it does not refresh on its own while open.
- A Hub upgrade that breaks a query is surfaced on the panel, not prevented.
- Limits 10 s per query and 10,000 rows per result stay; the drive measures a regex over every trace span on a copy of the operator's database and the numbers are revisited from that (2026-11-13).
- No separate design round: the screen is built as real components shown first in the mock (hub/ui/mock), which the operator reviews as the look (2026-11-13).
- A read-only query includes SELECT with recursive CTEs; only writes, schema changes and attach are refused.

Why responsiveness is its own requirement: on 2026-11-13 the operator's database holds 263,000 trace spans in a 920 MB file, and ordinary reads already take 1.5-3 s during night builds. A regex over every span is the heaviest read anyone will ask for; it must not add to that.

Hazard (Tier 2): storing dashboards adds a table, so the operator's :8000 Hub runs a migration on its real database at its next restart after this lands on master. The migration only creates a new table; rollback is its downgrade dropping it, which loses only saved dashboards. The migration's number is taken at build time from master's head (0176_spec_tag.py on 2026-11-13); if another migration lands first, re-point the down-revision before landing.

THE CONTRACT (snake_case MCP tools, `/projects/{project_id}/...` routes on `project_resources_router` in hub/hub/api/v1/__init__.py, prefixed ids, `sse_manager.broadcast(project_id, event_type, data)`):

Table `dashboards` (model `Dashboard` in hub/hub/db/models.py), project-scoped so the project-delete sweep reaches it with no code: `id` String(64) pk, `dash-` + 12 hex; `project_id` String(64) indexed; `name` String(200); `description` Text; `panels` JSON; `author` String(32) (from the run credential, never the request body); `created_at`, `updated_at`. Unique index (project_id, name).

Panel JSON: `{"id": "pnl-<12 hex>", "title": str, "query": str, "kind": "number" | "table" | "bar" | "stacked_bar" | "line"}`. The Hub assigns `id` when omitted and keeps it on replace. Any other kind: 422 `{"code": "invalid_chart_kind"}`.

Settings (hub/hub/config.py): `aw_dashboard_query_timeout: int = 10`, `aw_dashboard_query_max_rows: int = 10000`.

Query service: hub/hub/dashboard_query.py, `async def run_query(project_id, sql) -> QueryResult` = `{"columns", "rows", "row_count", "truncated", "elapsed_ms"}`. Refusals: 422 `{"detail": {"code": "not_queryable" | "read_only" | "timeout" | "query_error", "message"}}`.

Routes under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}` (hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py): GET /dashboards/query-reference; POST /dashboards/query; GET /dashboards; POST /dashboards (409 dashboard_name_taken); PUT /dashboards/{id}; GET /dashboards/{id}; GET /dashboards/{id}/run (per panel columns, rows, truncated, error, warning; one failing panel does not fail the rest); DELETE /dashboards/{id}. Another project's id is 404.

Agent tools (hub/hub/mcp_server.py): dashboard_query_reference(), run_dashboard_query(sql), save_dashboard(name, description, panels, dashboard_id=""), list_dashboards(), read_dashboard(dashboard_id). No agent delete. Added to the Copilot allowlist in hub/hub/copilot_acp.py.

Events: dashboard_saved, dashboard_deleted `{"id", "name"}` after commit.

UI: tab `dashboards` appended at the end of PROJECT_TABS (hub/ui/src/lib/navigation.ts; ThreadScreen.test.tsx asserts the order, not relaxed); components in hub/ui/src/components/dashboards, shown in hub/ui/mock/screens/Dashboards.tsx; hooks in hub/ui/src/api/dashboards.ts with keys ['project', projectId, 'dashboards', ...]. No charting library is added unless the builder justifies it.

open_questions.question: May a table panel show matched free text in full? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): yes, in full, nothing masked.
Is the screen designed first in a separate mock round? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): no; real components shown in the mock first, reviewed there.
Are 10 s per query and 10,000 rows the right limits? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): keep both; the drive measures a regex over all spans and they are revisited from that.
Is the task plan right? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): yes; DeveloperOpus2 builds the query service, Developer the screen, QA2 checks.
Does saving run the queries? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): no; save checks the chart kind and the never-queryable boundary, a failing panel shows its error on open.
When is the vault note seeded? Answer (operator, 2026-11-13): in every project at Hub startup and project creation, idempotently, never overwriting agents' additions.

problem: Questions about how the project is going — how much each spec cost, how often QA sends each model's work back, which kinds of task take longest, how many times something appears in the conversations — have no screen, although the Hub records everything needed to answer them. Today an answer is a one-off query an agent runs by hand, and it is lost with the conversation. This slice proves the loop the roadmap rests on: ask, get a dashboard with correct numbers in the app's look, reopen it later, and see it current.

requirements.rationale: An agent that cannot see what its query returns saves wrong numbers with confidence.
requirements.statement: Any agent can run a read-only query over the current project's data and receive its columns and rows, so it can check a query's result before it saves a dashboard.

requirements.rationale: One database holds every project on the Hub; the roadmap is heading towards other users' projects.
requirements.statement: A query never returns a row belonging to another project, whatever the query text says, including queries that omit a project filter, join tables, or read the list of projects.

A query cannot read credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers) or this machine's paths (the project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints); a query naming them is refused with a message saying what is not queryable.
A query cannot change any data: an insert, update, delete, schema change or attach is refused and the data is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The operator wants to count leaks and occurrences of things in the conversations.
requirements.statement: Free-text data is queryable — agent output, the traces' tool arguments and results, model messages and command lines, and message, queue and checkpoint text — and a query can match a regular expression against any text column.
A query that runs longer than 10 seconds is stopped and answers an error saying so, and a result over 10,000 rows is cut to 10,000 and says it was cut.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-11-13 ordinary reads already take 1.5-3 s during builds on a 920 MB database; the heaviest read anyone will ask for must not add to that.
requirements.statement: While dashboard queries run — including a regular-expression search over every trace span and a query stopped at the time limit — the Hub's event loop never stalls for more than 100 ms, and a GET /agents made meanwhile answers within 500 ms on a copy of the operator's database.

requirements.rationale: A hand-written description goes stale on the first migration.
requirements.statement: The Hub provides agents a reference of everything a query can reach — each table and column, its type and a short meaning — generated from the running version, and nothing in it is refused when queried.

Every project's vault holds a note on what the data means and its traps, present before any dashboard tool is first called — including in projects registered before this ships — and never overwritten once agents have added to it; the agent tools point agents to it, and it is seeded with the known traps (a send-back rejects every piece of evidence from that commit; cost per spec counts its tasks' building and reviewing runs).

requirements.rationale: A Hub upgrade can break a saved query anyway, so a failing panel has to be handled on the screen regardless.
requirements.statement: An agent can save a dashboard to the current project with a name, a description of the question it answers, and panels, each with a title, a query and a chart kind; the dashboard records which agent made it and when, and survives a Hub restart. Saving checks chart kinds and the never-queryable boundary but does not run the queries, so a panel whose query fails can be saved.
A panel's chart kind is one of a fixed set — single number, table, bar, stacked bar and line — and every kind is drawn in the app's colours and type, readable in both light and dark themes.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-13: the screen is local, and a masked leak cannot be found.
requirements.statement: A table panel shows every value its query returns in full, free text included; no value is masked or redacted.

The project has a Dashboards screen, reachable from the app's navigation, listing its dashboards with name, author and date; opening one runs all its queries and draws them, a Refresh button runs them again, and the dashboard shows when its data was last fetched. The operator can delete a dashboard there.

A panel whose query fails shows the error on that panel, and a panel whose result cannot be drawn as its chart kind (for example a line with no numeric column) shows a warning saying why; the other panels still draw.
Deleting a project removes its dashboards.

in_scope: Agent tools to read the query reference, run a read-only query and see its rows, and save, list and read dashboards
A Dashboards screen per project: list, open, refresh, delete
Panels: a title, a query and a chart kind from a fixed set, drawn in the app's style
Errors and warnings shown per panel
Queries that never stall the rest of the Hub
A vault note for what the data means, seeded in every project with the gotchas already known
non_goals: Changing a saved dashboard by asking (slice change-by-asking); in this slice an agent saves a new dashboard or replaces one whole
Stored tables, materialised or reusable named datasets
Queries across projects, or any write to project data
Agent-written chart code or styles outside the app's look
Masking or redacting values a query returns
Refreshing on a timer or as runs finish
Keeping saved queries working across Hub upgrades

summary: Any agent, asked in a conversation, writes queries over the current project's data (traces and free text included), checks their results, and saves a dashboard of panels drawn in the app's own chart kinds and colours. The project gets a Dashboards screen that lists them; opening one runs its queries, a Refresh button runs them again, and a panel whose query fails shows the error while the rest draws. Queries never slow the rest of the Hub. The Hub publishes a reference of what can be queried, generated from the running version, and a vault note in every project holds what agents learn about what the data means.

tasks.description: ac-examples fails on every run so far: 3 by the builders and 1 by QA2 at fbfc0cd. The Haiku analyst gets 'cost per spec' right, mostly; once it added a filter that matched nothing. It gets the other two panels wrong in the same way every time. (1) QA send-backs per model: it counts each move to revision_needed under the model of the run that made the move (the reviewer), so it gets {claude-opus-5-5: 4} where the drive's reference_send_backs_per_model gets {haiku-4-5: 2, opus-5-5: 1, sonnet-5-5: 1}. The reference attributes each send-back to the model of the run behind the task's latest move to completed (task_transitions.run_id joined to turn_usage). (2) Longest kinds of task: it averages per run (1068/612.5/254) where the reference first sums each task's runs and then averages per kind (2670/1225/1270). Fix this in what the agent is told, not in the drive: add the traps to the seeded data-meaning vault note and/or to the query reference's column meanings. Say what task_transitions.run_id is (the run that made the move, so a send-back's run is the reviewer's) and how to attribute work to the builder's model. Say that per-task totals are summed from runs before averaging per kind. The note must stay idempotent and never overwrite agents' additions. Then run scripts/drive/dashboards_drive.py --part main until ac-examples passes, and record its evidence for FR-11.
